title: Package Tree  -  as of 2026-07-04, second pass

canonical_node.axiom: The package tree is the authoritative inventory of all files in the Theophysics package, organized by category, with explicit status flags for known issues and pending moves.
definitions: Package tree: the directory listing and file organization as documented in this file.
Status flag: a marker indicating a known issue () or pending action (e.g., 'currently open in Excel').
Second pass: the second revision of this tree, dated 2026-07-04.
derivation: The document enumerates all files under each category folder.
It marks files with known issues using  and notes pending moves.
It includes an archive section for duplicates and a root section for unfiled files.
canonical_node.action: Maintain this tree as the single source of truth for file locations and statuses; update it when files are moved, added, or issues are resolved.
boundary: It does not define the content or correctness of the files themselves.
It does not resolve the flagged issues (e.g., gravity equation error, Law-2 mismatch).
It does not provide derivation or proof of any physical or theological claims.
test: Check that every file listed exists at the stated path.
Check that status flags match the actual state of the files (e.g., unresolved issues still flagged).
Check that pending moves (e.g., Master_Axiom.xlsx) are updated when completed.

dg1_dependencies: The actual file system of the package
dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a structured inventory and status overview of the entire package, enabling quick navigation and issue tracking.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the ability to locate any file and know its current status, even if the underlying content changes.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: Without this tree, file locations and known issues become undocumented, leading to confusion and potential loss of context.

classification.recommended_atom_action: maintain as living inventory; do not treat as evidence for physical or theological claims

overstatement_risks: Treating the tree as proof of the correctness of the files it lists.
Assuming that the absence of a  flag implies the file is error-free.
Using the tree to infer the validity of the underlying theories.
kill_conditions: If the tree becomes inconsistent with the actual file system.
If status flags are not updated when issues are resolved.
If the tree is used to assert the truth of the package's content.
risk.lean_target: No Lean target; this is a documentation artifact, not a mathematical claim.

plain_summary: This document is a file inventory for the Theophysics package, listing files by category and flagging known issues. It is useful for organization but does not establish any physical or theological truth.
